NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The proposed intervention is a thermal-gradient-aware balancing algorithm that adjusts balancing current based on cell temperature to mitigate series string imbalance drift. Standard practice applies a fixed balancing current regardless of thermal conditions; this intervention dynamically modulates balancing current in response to real-time temperature measurements to counteract the temperature-dependent self-discharge variation. The closest existing practice is passive cell balancing, which uses fixed resistors to bleed charge; this differs by actively balancing based on thermal state rather than fixed bleeds. The intervention attacks the failure's driving physics by balancing cells more aggressively in hotter regions where self-discharge is higher, preventing the capacity spread from growing beyond the threshold.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is the Arrhenius equation for self-discharge rate: k = A·e^(-Ea/RT), where k is the rate constant, A is the pre-exponential factor, Ea is activation energy, R is the gas constant, and T is temperature in Kelvin. A 15°C temperature difference (e.g., 298K vs 313K) can cause a 2-3x difference in self-discharge rates for NMC-811 chemistry. By increasing balancing current proportionally to cell temperature, we reduce the capacity spread (ΔC) at a rate of ΔC ∝ (k_hot - k_cold)·t, where t is time. This maintains the voltage spread below 35 mV by compensating for the thermal-driven divergence in state-of-charge.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — 
- (a) Existing BMS controller firmware (modified with new balancing algorithm)
- (a) Existing temperature sensors (already present in the module)
- (a) Existing balancing circuits (no hardware changes)
- (c) New balancing procedure: Temperature-dependent balancing current modulation (0.5-1.5A based on cell temperature, with 1A nominal)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — 
Standard practice uses: (a) BMS controller, (a) temperature sensors, (a) balancing circuits, (c) fixed 1A balancing procedure. This intervention adds only a firmware modification (c) and uses existing components. The burden is identical to standard practice—same hardware, same installation effort, same maintenance requirements. No additional cost, weight, or complexity is introduced.

EXECUTABLE TEST — 
Protocol: Cycle the module with 15°C top-to-bottom thermal gradient while monitoring cell voltages and temperatures. Apply the thermal-gradient-aware balancing algorithm for 10,000 cycles (simulating 10 years). Instruments: Voltage monitoring accuracy ±1mV, temperature monitoring accuracy ±0.5°C. Pass/fail threshold: maximum cell-to-cell voltage spread remains below 35 mV at rest after cycling. Duration: 10,000 cycles or equivalent calendar aging. Kill criterion: If voltage spread exceeds 35 mV at any point, the test fails and the intervention is falsified.
